justification: Critical, not Standard: this changes which provisions exist on the new side of every DCP extraction diff, for every council, on the path that feeds dcp_review_queue and therefore what a human can approve into regulatory_provisions. Before the fix a provision could cease to exist with every count agreeing; after it, provisions that previously vanished now appear as review rows. A mistake here either invents a provision the document does not contain (if identical duplicates were suffixed) or keeps losing real clauses (if the suffixing is wrong), and both reach served law. Standard was considered and rejected because the blast radius is every chapter of every council, not one council's alerting.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured on production read-only before writing any code, from the city_of_sydney re-read of the 1 Oct PDFs sitting in dcp_review_queue. (1) The extractor's own review file records `schedules: 605 sections | 0 tables | 605 provisions` with `0 unchanged | 28 changed | 423 added | 20 removed`, and `section-3-general-provisions: 1464 provisions` with `0 unchanged | 13 changed | 1226 added | 81 removed`. (2) Rows actually in the queue at the chapter's current content_hash: schedules 471 (451 carrying new_text = 423+28), section-3 1,320 (1,239 = 1226+13). (3) So 605-451 = 154 and 1464-1239 = 225 emitted provisions reached nothing: 379 across two chapters in one run. (4) All queue rows at the current hash are status 'pending'; none were auto-rejected, so no other status accounts for the gap. (5) Both chapters are `[RESTRUCTURE (full replace needed)]` with 0 unchanged, so every emitted provision should have produced a row.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Three assumptions of mine did not survive, and each is recorded because the wrong one was nearly shipped. (a) I first wrote a clause-coverage check in page_coverage.py that fingerprints lettered clause markers in the PDF and asserts each appears in the output. Measured against the real PDFs it found 7 clause markers in schedules where page 39 alone prints fifteen: PyMuPDF puts the marker on its own line ('(a) ') with the text in a separate block, so an anchored marker+text pattern matches almost nothing. It would NOT have caught the defect it was written for. Reverted. (b) A line-level absence variant did find the missing clause but reported 14-21% of PDF lines absent, which cannot be attributed between real loss, un-enqueued provisions and non-rule text, so it is not a gate. (c) Most importantly: I first wrote the accounting guard as total_new == unchanged+changed+renumbered+added and claimed in the code comment that it 'would have failed by 154 the moment it ran'. That was wrong. The overwrite deleted the provision from new_provisions BEFORE total_new was taken, so that identity held perfectly while 379 provisions were missing. The guard that catches it had to compare against new_sections instead. Both the comment and the guard were corrected before commit.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reuses existing concepts and adds no new module, column or query. The suffix form `_2` is exactly what ai_extractor.dedupe_provisions' docstring already said happened downstream ('the extractor downstream already suffixes a repeated number whose text differs (_2)') — that claim was false and this makes it true, rather than inventing a convention. Sameness is judged with the module's existing `_normalize_for_diff`, the same predicate the unchanged/changed decision already uses, so a whitespace-only repeat is one clause by the same rule everywhere. The raise follows the file's existing fail-loud contract (count_drop, section-loss guard) rather than adding a new alerting path.
pre_impl.external_source_error: The trigger is a council document whose own structure defeats the key. City of Sydney schedules 7.4 prints a list (a)-(o) and then restarts (a)(b)(c) under a 'Pedestrians' sub-heading INSIDE the same section, which is lawful drafting and not an error on their side. Nothing about the council's PDF can be fixed; the key had to stop assuming a clause letter is unique within a section. A council republishing (the 1 Oct PDFs) is what exposed it, because a full restructure makes every provision pass through the colliding path at once.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A — no TypeScript, TSX or frontend file is touched. The change is confined to one Python function and one pytest file, so no DB-to-API or API-to-component boundary is crossed. Served rows gain refs of the shape `..._7_4 (a)_2`, which the serve path renders from `section_ref` as any other ref; no renderer change is required and none is made.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a reader of a City of Sydney property report was shown section 7.4's transport requirements with two of the council's clauses missing — 'The ability of the public transport network to service the site in the peak and off peak and weekend periods' and 'Mode share targets' — while three refs carried a different list's text. Both missing strings are printed on PDF page 39 and appear nowhere in the 2,069 queued rows. There was no way to notice: page coverage passed, the emitted clause letters ran a-o with no gaps, total_new agreed with the diff, and the fidelity gate's section_collapsed flag pointed at the symptom (a shrunken parent) rather than the cause. After: both provisions exist as review rows a person can approve, and a future recurrence raises rather than passing silently.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: A repeated ref overwrites instead of being suffixed; identical text under a repeated ref starts being suffixed (inventing a provision); the collapse counter stops being incremented so the emitted-vs-kept equality under-reports; whitespace-only differences stop counting as the same clause; or the matching logic loses a provision already in new_provisions.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Two source mutations, both forced on purpose and both killed, then restored green. MUTATION A — delete `collapsed_duplicates += 1`: 3 tests fail and the failure carries the REAL guard's own wording, confirmed by grepping the output for 'unaccounted for' and 'AssertionError', so the production guard is what refuses rather than a test-side recomputation. MUTATION B — restore the original bare `new_provisions[ref] = ...` overwrite: 8 of 12 fail. Restored: 12 passed. Full suite on this branch: 7,586 passed, 2 skipped, 3 xfailed, 632 deselected, 0 failed. Note that the emitted-vs-kept guard cannot be forced to fire at runtime — given the code every section is either kept or counted, which is precisely the property it asserts — so it is forced by mutating the source, and the test that covers it says so rather than pretending otherwise.
falsifiable_check.not_proven: PENDING REAL-DATA VERIFICATION. Whether the fix actually recovers the two named clauses can only be shown by re-running the extraction, because the model's raw response is not stored and cannot be replayed. A `--review --all --council city_of_sydney --chapter schedules` run is in flight; until it reports, the claim 'this recovers 7.4(b) and 7.4(c)' is reasoned from the mechanism, not measured. Also not proven: that 379 is entirely explained by ref collision rather than partly by some other drop between emit and enqueue — the arithmetic fits and the 7.4 case is confirmed by hand, but the per-provision attribution for all 379 has not been done. Separately unaddressed by design: the extraction still gives the Pedestrians list the parent section's number, so `7_4 (a)_2` is citable and unique but its clause letter does not match the council's printed letter for that sub-list; naming sub-headings correctly is a different change and is not in this branch.

functions.name: diff_provisions
functions.input: new_sections (the extractor's emitted section dicts), document_id. Exercised on: two sections sharing a ref with differing text, three sharing one ref, a repeated ref with byte-identical text, a repeated ref differing only in whitespace, distinct refs, and build_ref_number monkeypatched to a constant so every section collides.
functions.output: new_provisions keyed by a ref unique within the chapter: the first occurrence keeps the plain ref, each later differing occurrence takes the lowest free `_N` suffix, and a later identical occurrence is dropped with collapsed_duplicates incremented.
functions.if_none: A section with an empty or missing section_number is not special-cased here and never was — build_ref_number maps 'preamble' explicitly and anything else by replacing dots, so it always returns a string. The None-ish case that matters is `_normalize_for_diff` on a null text: it is the same call the unchanged/changed branch already makes on old_prov['text'], so a null-vs-null repeat compares equal and collapses rather than raising.

values.name: the duplicate-ref suffix
values.read_at: scripts/dcp_extract_changed.py, inside the new_sections loop; asserted by test_the_second_is_suffixed_not_overwritten and test_three_provisions_on_one_ref.
values.if_missing: Not configurable, deliberately. It is the form ai_extractor.dedupe_provisions' docstring already names, so making it settable would let two parts of the pipeline disagree about what a repeated ref looks like. The loop takes the lowest unused suffix rather than a counter so that re-running on the same input produces the same refs — a changing ref is itself the defect this file has fought before (the Marrickville re-key churn).

break_it.scenario: The model emits the same clause twice with identical text (a chunk boundary read twice).
break_it.what_happens: The second is collapsed, not suffixed, so no phantom provision is created; collapsed_duplicates counts it so the emitted-vs-kept equality still reconciles.
break_it.how: Sameness uses the module's existing `_normalize_for_diff`, the same predicate the unchanged/changed decision uses, so whitespace-only repeats collapse too. Asserted by test_identical_text_is_still_collapsed and test_whitespace_only_difference_is_the_same_clause; deleting the counter turns both red along with the equality test.
break_it.repro: Two sections, same section_number, same content: total_new == 1.

break_it.scenario: A council's chapter legitimately repeats a clause letter across two sub-lists, and a later re-extraction orders them differently.
break_it.what_happens: Which occurrence gets the plain ref and which gets `_2` could swap, producing a spurious `changed` pair on the next diff.
break_it.how: NOT mitigated, and stated rather than hidden. The suffix follows document order, which is stable for a stable PDF, but an LLM reader is not order-guaranteed across runs. The cost is review churn on those rows, not wrong served text — and the previous behaviour's cost was losing the provision outright, which is strictly worse. The durable fix is keying sub-lists by their own sub-heading, which is named in not_proven and is not in this branch.
break_it.repro: Feed the two colliding sections in the opposite order; the `_2` lands on the other one.

break_it.scenario: A chapter with hundreds of collisions raises mid-run.
break_it.what_happens: diff_provisions raises AssertionError naming the shortfall, so that one chapter fails its run instead of enqueueing a diff that is quietly short of provisions.
break_it.how: The extraction loop already catches per-chapter exceptions and continues to the next chapter (observed in the 1 Oct run, where every chapter failed with RateLimitError in turn and the batch completed with a summary). A failed chapter retains needs_extraction=TRUE for retry, so the outcome is a visible failure and a retry, never a partial commit. The raise is the file's existing fail-loud contract, not a new one.
break_it.repro: Mutate away the collapse counter and run any colliding input; the chapter raises and the message names the shortfall.

break_it.scenario: The suffixed ref reaches the served set and a report cites `7.4 (a)_2`.
break_it.what_happens: A reader sees a ref that is not literally how the council prints the clause.
break_it.how: NOT fully mitigated. The ref is unique and resolvable, and the page link still points at the council's page, but the printed clause letter for the Pedestrians sub-list is the sub-list's own (a), not `7.4 (a)_2`. This is a citation-presentation gap, strictly better than the clause being absent, and the correct fix is sub-heading-aware keying. Flagged here so it is not discovered by a reader.
break_it.repro: Approve a suffixed row and view the provision in a report.

break_it.scenario: A chapter where the collision is between a real clause and a TABLE row or figure caption the reader also labelled '(a)'.
break_it.what_happens: Both are kept under `(a)` and `(a)_2`, so a figure caption can become a provision-shaped row instead of being dropped.
break_it.how: Partly, and by machinery that already exists rather than anything added here: the row still passes through classify_row_fidelity and _serious_artifacts on the way to the queue, and an emptied or junk-keyed row is auto-rejected there. What this change guarantees is only that the row is VISIBLE instead of silently replacing a real clause — a junk row a person rejects is strictly better than a real clause disappearing, which is the directionality rule in memory/project-defect-repair-calibration-2026-08.md (approving chooses values, rejecting cannot create a false claim).
break_it.repro: Two sections with section_number '(a)', one real clause text and one caption; both appear as rows and the caption is judged by the existing gate.

post_merge.db_reset: No migration and no backfill. But NOTE: the existing 2,069 pending city_of_sydney rows were produced by the OLD code and are missing the provisions this fix recovers. They must not be approved. A re-extract deletes a chapter's pending rows and inserts fresh ones (dcp_extract_changed.py ~L2969), so the correct action is to re-run both chapters on this code and review the replacement diff.
post_merge.manual_verify: YES. (1) Re-run `--review --all --council city_of_sydney` for both chapters on this code and confirm the run reports no accounting shortfall. (2) Confirm 'The ability of the public transport network to service the site' and 'Mode share targets' now appear in dcp_review_queue for schedules — they are printed on PDF page 39 and were absent from all 2,069 old rows. (3) Expect MORE review rows than before, because provisions that previously vanished now appear; that is the fix working, not a regression. (4) DQ-70 (133 rules) and DQ-113 (133 unchecked) and OC-10 still clear only on a human approval plus dcp-commit, and both chapters must commit because DQ-70 counts 87 from section-3 and 46 from schedules.
